entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Lancelotto Malocello was an Italian navigator and citizen of the Republic of Genoa, born around 1280, who gave his name to the island of Lanzarote, one of the Canary Islands.

Malocello's voyage to the Canary Islands in 1312-1313 is considered one of the earliest European expeditions to the Atlantic Ocean.

The expedition's significance lies in its demonstration of the navigational skills and entrepreneurial spirit of the Genoese, who established a thriving trading network in the Atlantic during the 14th century.

Malocello's legacy extends to the naming of the island of Lanzarote, which has become a major tourist destination in the Canary Islands, and the recognition of the importance of Genoese navigation in the early Age of Exploration.

This island's volcanic landscapes, beaches, and unique wildlife have made it a popular destination for tourists, scientists, and explorers, cementing Malocello's place in history as a pioneering navigator and entrepreneur.

As we look back on Malocello's remarkable journey, we are reminded of the power of human curiosity, determination, and innovation in shaping our world.

Lanzarote's natural beauty, rich history, and cultural significance make it a fascinating destination that continues to inspire visitors from around the globe.

This island's story is a testament to the enduring legacy of Malocello and the Republic of Genoa, who left an indelible mark on the course of world history.
